newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police search for bodies in Sumatra serial murders.
newsitem.headline: Police search for bodies in Sumatra serial murders.

text.p: Indonesian police were searching on Monday for the remains of victims of a black magic practitioner who claims to have killed 42 women.

Police in the city of Medan in North Sumatra said the search was concentrated on a sugar plantation at the nearby village of Aman Damai, which means "peaceful and secure" in the Indonesian language, where skeletons of 19 women have already been found.

The sorcerer, Amat Suraji, 45, was arrested late last month after the father of one of his alleged victims told police his daughter disappeared after going to his house for treatment of an unspecified illness. He is being held on suspicion of murder, police said.

Suraji told police he had killed 42 women since 1986 in an effort to improve his powers, newspapers have reported. He said all his victims were strangled and buried semi-naked with their hands tied behind their backs.
His three wives, who are sisters, have also been arrested on suspicion of abetment.
Suraji told police he planned to kill 70 women to gain the ultimate power of healing, newspapers reported. He said he did not rape his victims.
"I killed the women only to improve my healing power," he was quoted as saying.
Police said the killings were not discovered for a long time because the victims were mostly prostitutes and their relatives were not concerned about their whereabouts.
